questionText: When fine-tuning an LLM (Large Language Model) using RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback), why is the Reward Model step critical before final policy optimization?
correctAnswer: It creates a proxy for human preferences the model can optimize against.
options: It expands the model's total parameter count for fine-tuning.
It creates a proxy for human preferences the model can optimize against.
It reduces inference cost by compressing transformer layer weights.
It restricts outputs to a predefined set of safe responses.
explanation: RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) requires a way to score model outputs. The Reward Model acts as a proxy for human judgment, allowing thousands of training iterations without human intervention.
remediationNotes: Review the 'RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) Workflow' in the Advanced Model Training section.
learningObjective: Explain the role of Reward Models in RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback).
option_a: It expands the model's total parameter count for fine-tuning.
option_b: It creates a proxy for human preferences the model can optimize against.
option_c: It reduces inference cost by compressing transformer layer weights.
option_d: It restricts outputs to a predefined set of safe responses.

questionText: In a transformer-based architecture, what is the primary function of the Multi-Head Attention mechanism?
correctAnswer: To attend to multiple representation subspaces simultaneously.
options: To accelerate individual floating-point CPU (Central Processing Unit) operations.
To attend to multiple representation subspaces simultaneously.
To store factual memories across long context windows.
To encrypt attention weights and prevent model extraction.
explanation: Multi-head attention enables the model to focus on different parts of the input sequence — such as grammar vs. context — at the same time.

learningObjective: Describe the mechanics of transformer attention heads.
option_a: To accelerate individual floating-point CPU (Central Processing Unit) operations.
option_b: To attend to multiple representation subspaces simultaneously.
option_c: To store factual memories across long context windows.
option_d: To encrypt attention weights and prevent model extraction.

questionText: Error analysis shows your model is underfitting — it performs poorly on both training and validation data. Which adjustment is most likely to reduce this high bias?
correctAnswer: Adding model complexity or improving feature engineering.
options: Increasing dropout rate to 0.9 to force more sparsity.
Adding model complexity or improving feature engineering.
Adding more L2 regularization to penalize large weights.
Reducing the training dataset to cut processing noise.
explanation: High bias (underfitting) means the model is too simple. Increasing complexity helps the model learn more nuanced patterns in the data.
remediationNotes: Review the 'Bias-Variance Tradeoff' in the advanced metrics section.
learningObjective: Identify solutions for high bias in deep learning.
option_a: Increasing dropout rate to 0.9 to force more sparsity.
option_b: Adding model complexity or improving feature engineering.
option_c: Adding more L2 regularization to penalize large weights.
option_d: Reducing the training dataset to cut processing noise.

questionText: When deploying a model using a Canary Deployment strategy, what is the primary risk mitigation benefit?
correctAnswer: Limits failure impact by first deploying to a small user subset.
options: Ensures both model versions run simultaneously on all traffic.
Limits failure impact by first deploying to a small user subset.
Increases server uptime by 50% over standard blue-green deployment.
Reduces cloud storage cost by purging all prior model versions.
explanation: Canary deployments allow for real-world monitoring with minimal blast radius if the new model version behaves unexpectedly.

questionText: In Adversarial Machine Learning, what specifically distinguishes an Evasion Attack from other attack types?
correctAnswer: Imperceptible input modifications that force the model to misclassify.
options: Deleting model weights from the server to disable access.
Imperceptible input modifications that force the model to misclassify.
Poisoning training data with fake examples until accuracy collapses.
Sending rapid API (Application Programming Interface) calls to crash the inference server (DDoS).
explanation: Evasion attacks exploit the model's decision boundaries by making subtle input changes, forcing errors without modifying the model itself.
remediationNotes: Review the 'AI (Artificial Intelligence) Security' section on adversarial attacks.
